title: PRD: Deterministic structured-emission rules, schema versioning, and tool-handshake recovery
creator: Asha Patel
description: High-level PRD that defines deterministic rules for emitting structured objects in both full-response and progressive (streamed) modes, establishes schema version negotiation semantics, and specifies recovery/handshake behavior for tool/function calls when partial objects, network failures, or parser errors occur.
background: Teams have reported inconsistent behavior when models emit partially-formed JSON or when schema versions differ between the model and a downstream tool. There is ambiguity around: (1) when to close a streamed object, (2) how to record and surface partial outputs to callers, (3) how retries should behave across idempotent vs non-idempotent tool calls, and (4) how clients and server negotiate schema version compatibility. This PRD consolidates product decisions into deterministic acceptance criteria and test cases.
goals: Define a single authoritative emit-state machine for structured outputs across streaming and non-streaming endpoints
Specify schema version negotiation and backward-compatible upgrade rules for models and toolkits
Define retry semantics and idempotency guarantees for tool/function invocation across partial emissions
Provide a clear set of acceptance tests and observability signals (metrics/logs) to validate correctness in production
non_goals: Changing the wire protocol (we'll keep current streaming framing semantics)
Re-implementing tool-side idempotency — only server-side guidance and wrappers are in scope
Support for arbitrarily nested streaming of different schema types in a single stream (out of scope for this phase)
acceptance_criteria: Emit-state machine: For any structured response endpoint, the server must expose a deterministic set of states: START, EMITTING_OBJECT, EMITTING_ARRAY, FIELD_PENDING, FIELD_COMPLETE, OBJECT_COMPLETE, STREAM_CLOSED, and ERROR. Transitions must be documented and implemented such that replaying the same token sequence yields identical state transitions.

Partial-object checkpointing: When streaming, the server must emit explicit checkpoint tokens that mark the boundary of a syntactically-valid partial object (example token: "__CHECKPOINT_v1__"). Clients must be able to apply the checkpointed partial object and resume parsing incrementally without heuristics.

Schema version negotiation: Each response that produces structured output must carry a schema_version header/field. If model/schema_version != client/expected_version, server must follow the negotiation policy: (a) exact match -> OK; (b) model_minor_backwards_compatible -> allow; (c) incompatible_major -> reject with structured error code 'SCHEMA_MISMATCH' and suggested_fallback_model(s).

Deterministic merge rules: When a streamed response contains multiple partial fragments for the same logical object (e.g., incremental enrichment), the server must include an explicit merge key and a deterministic merge strategy (first-write-wins, last-write-wins, or field-level merge). The merge strategy must be negotiable per-route and included in the session metadata.

Tool-handshake contract: Before invoking an external tool/function, the platform must perform a lightweight handshake: exchange tool_schema_version and capabilities. If the tool reports a non-overlapping schema, invocation must fail fast with 'TOOL_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE' and include recommended tool versions.

Idempotency tokens and retries: For any tool invocation that changes state, the platform must require an idempotency_key header. Retries are allowed only for invocations with idempotency_key present. For invocations without idempotency_key, retries must not be attempted automatically; instead client-friendly structured error code 'NON_IDEMPOTENT_NO_RETRY' should be emitted.

Partial-failure semantics: If a stream fails mid-object (network error, internal exception), the server should (a) emit a final structured error event containing last_successful_checkpoint, error_code, and a digest that uniquely identifies the partial object; (b) expose an API to resume from last_successful_checkpoint for up to 7 days for Dedicated customers (configurable).

Observable signals: Each acceptance test run must validate emitted metrics: structured_output.emitted_objects, structured_output.partial_checkpoints, tool.handshake.failures, tool.invocations.retries, and schema.negotiation.failures. Logs must include checkpoint sequence IDs to correlate traces.

Backward compatibility: Rolling the schema minor version must not break existing clients when the server documents the backward-compatible changes. Acceptance tests must include a client pinned to N observing data from a model emitting N+1 minor version and verifying no parsing errors occur.

Regression tests: The CI must run a suite of 30+ synthetic scenarios that cover: perfectly-formed streaming, partial-object then resume, malformed-json then graceful-recovery, tool-handshake mismatch, idempotent retry success, idempotent retry failure, and stream backpressure/drop followed by resume. All must pass with deterministic outcomes.
test_cases: TC-001: Streamed JSON object with two checkpoints; consumer resumes after checkpoint 1 and verifies rehydrated state
TC-002: Schema mismatch where model_major != client_major: expect SCHEMA_MISMATCH error and no tool invocation attempted
TC-003: Non-idempotent tool call without idempotency_key: expect NON_IDEMPOTENT_NO_RETRY and no automatic retry; manual retry should be possible with client confirmation
TC-004: Partial syntax error mid-field: server emits ERROR event with last_successful_checkpoint and a human-readable hint; client can request context for debugging
TC-005: Handshake failure with external tool returning older schema: platform suggests compatible tool versions and falls back to read-only simulation mode for the tool
open_decisions: Checkpoint token naming and escaping: engineering suggested __CP_v1__ but design wants fully JSON-wrapped sentinel objects - decision pending
Resume storage TTL: draft is 7 days for Dedicated customers, 30 minutes for Hosted free-tier. Ops feedback required on storage costs
Merge default strategy: choose last-write-wins for initial rollout; allow route-level override in later release
tradeoffs_and_risks: Adding explicit checkpoint tokens simplifies client parsing but slightly increases token usage and cost; risk acceptable for most customers but needs opt-out for ultra-low-cost flows
Enforcing idempotency_key for all mutating tool calls provides safety but increases client implementation burden; will provide SDK helpers to mitigate
Providing resume-from-checkpoint increases storage complexity and potential PII retention concerns; must be gated by encryption-at-rest and configurable TTL
implementation_notes: Runtime: implement emit-state machine as part of the tokenizer layer so streaming and non-streaming share logic
Console: add per-route toggle for 'enable_checkpointing' and visible schema_version in the route configuration UI
SDKs: add helper to generate idempotency_key and automatic handshake verification; fallback to descriptive errors if handshake fails
Ops: add a new retention policy and encryption verification for resume blobs; plan migration path for Dedicated customers
